title: What Is System Design?
intro: System design is planning how the parts of a software system fit together so it stays fast, reliable and affordable as it grows. This series builds it up one concept at a time.

slides.heading: The big picture
slides.subtitle: Designing the whole system, not one function.
slides.explain: Coding answers "how do I build this feature?". System design answers "how do servers, databases, caches and queues work together for millions of users?"
points: Decide how they talk to each other

slides.heading: Functional needs
slides.subtitle: What the system must do.
slides.explain: These are the features users see. List them first, because every design decision should serve one of them.
points: Users can sign up and log in

slides.heading: Non-functional needs
slides.subtitle: How well the system must do it.
slides.explain: These qualities shape the architecture. Two apps with the same features can need very different designs because of them.

slides.heading: Estimate the scale
slides.subtitle: Back-of-the-envelope math.
slides.explain: Rough numbers tell you whether one server is enough or you need hundreds. You only need the right order of magnitude, not exact figures.
points: 10M daily users x 10 requests = 100M requests a day
That's about 1,150 requests per second on average
Peaks can be several times higher

slides.heading: Trade-offs
slides.subtitle: There is no perfect design.
slides.explain: Faster reads can mean slower writes, and more consistency can mean less availability. Good design means choosing the right trade-off and explaining why.

scenario.situation: A team builds a photo app without writing down requirements or estimating traffic.
scenario.problem: It runs on one server and one database. A viral post brings 50x the usual traffic and the whole app goes down.
scenario.fix: Start with requirements and rough numbers. Knowing the expected peak would have shown the need for caching and more servers before launch.
scenario.takeaway: Requirements and estimates come before architecture.
